newsitem.title: USA: US March T-bonds close down, post outside-down day.
newsitem.headline: US March T-bonds close down, post outside-down day.

text.p: U.S. debt futures traded higher early but slumped midday to end lower, under pressure from corporate supply and renewed worries of inflation.

The largest investment-grade corporate debt deal ever -- a US West Capital Funding $4.1 billion multi-tranche offering -- was priced near midday. Near then, Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said he saw a risk of higher inflation.

"I have slightly greater concern that inflation will increase than that the economy will lapse into persistent, below-trend growth and face rising employment," Meyer said in a speech in Charlotte, N.C.
Traders said technicals woes were beginning to beset U.S. March T-bonds.
March poked to nearly a two-week high early in the day but dipped below Wednesday's session low and closed below there. Technicians called it an outside-down day and a bearish technical reversal.
Traders noted a rush of sell-stops below 111-00.
Paul Hare, technician with LIT's The Linn Group in Chicago, said the outside-down day confirmed that the market -- while rangebound -- was headed to the lower end of that range.
"We have an outside-down day which at least puts the market short-term on the defensive," agreed Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager with ED&F Man.
"But we also had an outside-up day last Thursday and the employment number negated that move, so I'm not sure how much importance it is going to have," Pullen added.
He said long-liquidation was noted below 111-00, and put support at 110-12/32 and 110-00.
Several traders said the market could be in for continued range action, perhaps between the low 1110-00 to 112-00 handles.

"There's a reluctance to buy the market until you see the employment cost index at the end of the month," a bond options trader said. "People are still worried about the economy picking up and they've got to see more numbers before they're too willing to buy it," he said.
Traders initally shrugged off a larger-than-expected drop in the latest weekly jobless claims, but paid more attention to a strong Philadelphia Fed business activity index.
Claims for the January 11 week fell to 323,000 from a revised 355,000 in the prior week. Philly Fed rose to 11.3 in January from a revised minus 6.2 in December.

At settlement, March T-bonds were off 18/32 to 110-23/32, T-notes lost 9/32 to 108-8/32, muni-bonds lost 17/32 to 114-12/32, T-bills lost three bps to 94.89, and June Eurodollars fell two bps to 94.17. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
